title: Integrated 1M-to-2M outcome-blind Slumbot-state drift
benchmark: A frozen learned policy plays at least 100,000 fresh 200bb HUNL Slumbot hands, scores above 0 bb/100, and has a 95% confidence-interval lower bound above 0.
hypothesis: The 2M endpoint's external decline is accompanied by a reproducible increase in high-exposure greedy disagreement from Standard10 relative to the 1M policy on both independent on-policy Slumbot state corpora, localizing a policy-preservation target rather than attributing the outcome to training scale alone.
material_change: Replay frozen Standard10, Seed1 1M, and Seed1 2M policies on every decision state from the independent audited 1M fresh20k and 2M fresh20k corpora. Use the trained legacy-v4 observation bridge, compare physical-action probability distributions and greedy actions, and stratify by corpus, seat, street, facing-bet, pot, SPR, and exposure. Never read hand outcomes into rows or make network calls.
baseline: 1M fresh20k was -21.7592 bb/100 CI [-44.2479,0.7295]; 2M fresh20k was -38.02 CI [-59.4244,-16.6156]. Internal combined 2M-minus-1M showed Standard10 -5.9489 and seat0 -4.8258 bb/100 with CI upper below zero, while synthetic Standard10 drift remained small.
source: Audited raw decision corpora and frozen SHAs from v6-integrated-seed1-1m-greedy-fresh20k-slumbot-20260903 and v6-integrated-seed1-2m-greedy-fresh20k-slumbot-20260903; Standard10 SHA 91b0c587, 1M SHA 6fbbe021, 2M SHA 993fe99b.
notes: Preregistered mechanism support requires 2M-minus-1M Standard10 stake-weighted greedy-disagreement increase >=0.005 on both on-policy corpora, 100% replay parity for the logged on-policy actions, and at least one supported seat/street/exposure partition showing the same direction. Failure means the external loss is not explained by this drift metric, not that training scale is sufficient.

The preregistered first replay selected CUDA and reproduced 124114/124121 logged CPU actions. Seven near-boundary mismatches invalidate its integrity gate. Original evidence and engine are preserved; a CPU-only wrapper will write to a new cpu/ directory without overwriting first-pass artifacts.

CPU batch-1024 replay reduced logged-action mismatch to 1/124121. The remaining state is a numerical batch-boundary argmax mismatch; all live session auditors already passed batch-size-one CPU replay. A new repair command will re-infer only mismatched rows for all three policies at batch size one and write new cpu_exact artifacts.

CPU-exact repair re-inferred the sole batch-boundary mismatch for all three policies at deployment batch size one. Final parity is 124121/124121; first CUDA and second CPU-batch artifacts remain immutable and explicitly non-admissible for the integrity gate.

result.summary: Outcome-blind replay evaluated Standard10, Seed1 1M, and Seed1 2M on 124121 audited decision states from two independent 20k Slumbot corpora. CPU-exact correction achieved 124121/124121 logged-action parity. The 2M-minus-1M Standard10 stake-weighted disagreement gap was -0.00465 on the 1M corpus and -0.00409 on the 2M corpus; direct 1M-versus-2M disagreement was about 1.04%.
result.conclusion: The preregistered high-exposure Standard10-drift mechanism is rejected. On both corpora the externally worse 2M policy was closer to Standard10 in mean TV and stake-weighted greedy behavior, not farther. Only preflop/small-pot disagreement increased about 0.5 percentage point. Therefore more source KL or a high-stakes preservation penalty is not evidence-based; simple distribution distance to Standard10 is externally misaligned here. Initial CUDA and batched-CPU parity failures were numerical audit-contract issues and were resolved without changing raw corpora.
result.next_step: Do not revive entropy sharpening, greedy-margin, direct-greedy ES, or 25%-public-opponent training, which have explicit negative evidence. Test whether a public-opponent reward objective can coexist geometrically with broad anchor-seat and source-preservation objectives at the retained 1M checkpoint using an offline multi-objective gradient feasibility audit. Only if a common descent direction exists should a bounded on-policy public-opponent-aware intervention be trained and evaluated across multiple seeds.
